rationale:
I judged the tests against `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection` by mapping each obligation to the supplied tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`. I did not request implementation source.

- **Resolution from the root against the retained outline, returning an owned `OutlineContent`.**
  - `fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]` selects every outline item. For each it asserts that `text()` equals the source span and that the structural hash matches.
  - `fn[markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items]` selects nested, duplicate (`#1`/`#2`), anonymous and encoded selectors.
  - `fn[css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent]` selects numbered CSS duplicates.
  - `fn[selecting_multipart_impls_and_literal_slashes_preserves_label_boundaries]` selects multipart `impl` labels, and it also selects `fn[run]` below one.
  - Empty-selector (root) selection is covered by `fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]` and by the root checks in the Rust and unicode tests.
  - Selecting from an already-selected (non-root) handle resolves from the file root. The Markdown test checks `second.select(main)`.
- **Sharing the source snapshot and fingerprinting rules.**
  - The Rust and Markdown tests assert `std::ptr::eq(selected.outline(), contents.outline())`.
  - `fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` checks that the language, fingerprint scheme and fingerprint are retained by selected items. The selected structural hash is also checked.
  - `fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]` checks the `fingerprint().scheme` format.
- **No additional file read, and usable after the original handle is dropped.** `fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]` drops `file` and rewrites the file on disk. It then asserts that `selected_again.text()` is unchanged. It also asserts that `selected.select("")` still returns the original root text, and that a fresh `from_id` now fails. That shows the retained snapshot is used and the file is not re-read.
- **Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable.**
  - `fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` asserts that the two `alpha` lines have the same selector and that selecting it yields `alpha`.
  - `fn[ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines]` asserts that identical `same` lines select successfully.
- **Invalid, missing and ambiguous selections return errors.**
  - `fn[missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors]` covers the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing item `fn[absent]`.
  - `fn[ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines]` covers an ambiguous non-line kind and a `line` kind with differing hashes. Both must return errors containing "ambiguous".
  - The CSS test asserts that the un-numbered `rule[a%20b]` errors.
  - The multipart and literal-slash test asserts that `impl[Thing%2Fcore::fmt::Display]` and `section[A/B]` error.
- **`id()` and `text()`.**
  - `id()` is asserted for selected and root handles in `fn[selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits]`.
  - `text()` is the original text, including attached doc comments and attributes, in the Rust test. It is also the pre-redaction raw text in `fn[formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans]`.

The selector-syntax and error requirements are cited context. The tests apply them to selection in the cases above. I found no unmapped obligation and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
